transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

For about the past 10 months, I've been experiencing really extreme mood swings where I feel abnormally happy and euphoric one moment, but then suddenly get incredibly irritable. I also have this overwhelming amount of energy all the time that I just can't seem to shake.

Have you ever had times when you heard or saw things ուրիշ people didn’t, or had very strong beliefs that others said were not true? If so, did those happen only during mood episodes or also when your mood was normal?
No, I've never experienced hearing or seeing things that other people couldn't. I also haven't ever held any strong beliefs that others found untrue or argued with me about.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where your mood was abnormally elevated or irritable and your energy was so high that you needed much less sleep, felt much more active or talkative, or had risky behavior that caused major problems?

Yes, I've been experiencing exactly that for about 10 months now. I feel overflowing with energy and constantly hyperactive, to the point where I just can't stay still. My mood constantly switches between feeling incredibly euphoric and then suddenly getting easily irritated.
Have you also had any periods of at least 2 weeks where you felt very depressed, lost interest or pleasure in things, or had low energy and slowed down?
No, I have never experienced periods of feeling depressed, losing interest, or having low energy. On the contrary, I have mostly felt extremely energized and active over the past 10 months.

This supports Bipolar I Disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a 10-month period of abnormally elevated/euphoric and irritable mood with persistently increased energy, hyperactivity, and likely manic symptoms lasting well over 1 week, with no history of major depressive episodes. He denies hallucinations and delusions, making a primary psychotic disorder or schizoaffective disorder less likely. The presentation is most consistent with Bipolar I Disorder.
